newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.S. offers reward for word about Kashmir hostage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. offers reward for word about Kashmir hostage.

text.p: The U.S. government on Wednesday offered a cash reward for information about an American hostage held by militants in Indian-ruled Kashmir.
U.S. Ambassador to Pakistan Thomas Simons announced the offer at a news conference in Islamabad. He did not specify the amount of the reward but said it would be substantial.

"Please come forward without further delay and tell us what you know," he said in his appeal for information about the whereabouts of Donald Hutchings, who has been held hostage along with two Britons and a German for more than a year.
"Your identity will be kept confidential and for your cooperation you may be eligible for a substantial sum of money by way of a reward," he said.

Hutchings and another American, John Childs, and Britons Keith Mangan and Paul Wells were kidnapped by the shadowy Al-Faran militant group while they were trekking in the Kashmiri mountains on July 4, 1995.
Childs escaped four days later, the same day Al-Faran also captured Norwegian Hans Christian Ostroe and German Dirk Hasert. A month later, Ostroe was found beheaded in a remote Kashmiri forest.
Negotiations between Indian officials and Al-Faran broke down last November.

Simons said the announcement for the reward was for "verifiable information" about Hutchings and applicable only for information given in Pakistan, but the U.S. government was working on a similar offer for India.

The four remaining hostages have since been sighted from time to time by local Kashmiris, including nomadic shepherds, but authorities have not been able to determine with certainty whether the captives are dead or alive.
Al-Faran is among dozens of groups fighting Indian rule over two-thirds of Kashmir ruled by New Delhi.
India accuses Islamabad of arming and training militants. Pakistan, which rules one-third of Kashmir and has staked a claim to the rest, denies the accusation.
